candidates.title: Vouchers and delegate-call vouchers above about 55 KB cannot be executed: Application.executeOutput costs about 290 gas per output byte, and no output above about 0.4-1 MB fits a transaction, while the rollup interface lets a guest commit outputs up to the 2 MiB tx buffer
candidates.component: cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application (output execution), pinned by Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7. Related: machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1 libcmt cmt_rollup_emit_voucher / emit_delegate_call_voucher (limit = tx buffer), and the manual's rollup interface.
candidates.role: Referee model (Dave and the rollups-contracts it pins, as the deployed referee, per the AUDIT.md table; output validation and execution is what the referee does to accept an output). Guest software (libcmt) only as the side that sets the bound.
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/dependencies/cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10/src/dapp/Application.sol executeOutput -> _executeOutput(bytes memory) -> LibBytes.consumeBytes4 (src/library/LibBytes.sol: a byte-by-byte copy loop `for (i < arguments.length) arguments[i] = buffer[i + 4]`) -> _executeVoucher / _executeDelegateCallVoucher (abi.decode copies the payload again). Size bound on the guest side: libcmt src/rollup.c cmt_rollup_emit_voucher/emit_delegate_call_voucher (only -ENOBUFS when the encoding exceeds the tx buffer); emulator AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_LOG2_SIZE = 21 (src/address-range-defines.h:48).
candidates.description: A correctly designed application (section 2: follows the rollup interface the manual specifies) may emit a voucher or delegate-call voucher of any length that fits the 2 MiB CMIO tx buffer; libcmt accepts it, hashes it into the outputs Merkle tree, and the settled state commits to it. The only way the deployed referee accepts (executes) a voucher is Application.executeOutput, a transaction that carries the whole output as calldata and spends, measured on the released artifact, about 290 gas of execution per output byte, almost all in LibBytes.consumeBytes4's per-byte copy (plus a second copy by abi.decode). Execution gas grows from 0.41 M at 1.2 KB to 13.4 M at 45 KB, 15.9 M at 53 KB, 17.1 M at 57 KB, 19.5 M at 66 KB, 39.6 M at 131 KB, 168 M at 524 KB and 815-829 M at 2 MiB. Under Ethereum's per-transaction gas cap (EIP-7825, 2^24 = 16,777,216 gas, active since Fusaka) every voucher above about 55 KB is therefore unexecutable for ever; under a 30-60 M block limit the bound is about 100-200 KB. Independently of the copy loop, the calldata alone (16 gas per nonzero byte, EIP-7623 floor 40 gas per nonzero byte, geth's 128 KiB txpool size limit) makes every output above roughly 0.4-1 MB unpresentable, so the gap between what a guest may commit to and what the referee can accept is a protocol bound, not only a gas optimization. Nothing (manual, libcmt, the emulator, the contracts) states or enforces a maximum output size that matches the referee. The asymmetry with inputs is explicit in the threat model: A3 makes the input record refuse inputs whose honest delivery proof would exceed the chain's per-transaction limits, but no rule refuses outputs that cannot be executed.
candidates.trigger: Any party that gets a correctly designed application to emit a large voucher: e.g. an input sender whose input makes the application emit a voucher carrying a large payload (a batched transfer, a payload echoed from the input up to the 64 KiB-ish input limit, or app-built data), or the application itself. After the epoch settles, every executeOutput for that output reverts with out-of-gas or is not includable; the output is committed and has a valid proof, but the referee never accepts it.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template running libcmt (or /usr/bin/rollup, rollup-http-server): emit a Voucher(address,uint256,bytes) whose ABI encoding is between ~55 KB and 2 MiB - the accept yield then writes the outputs root that includes it; the machine validity proof and stageTournamentResult/acceptStagedTournamentResult work as usual, so the root enters DaveConsensus._outputsMerkleRoots and validateOutput (a view, callable by eth_call with a large RPC gas cap) succeeds. Only the execution transaction fails. No unreachable state is involved.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Checked each exclusion against the trigger. 'An application that is not correctly designed' does not apply: section 2 defines a correctly designed application by following the rollup interface and bounding mcycles; the manual's rollup interface ('#### Rollup', 'Write ABI-encoded output to CMIO TX buffer and its length') and libcmt allow any output that fits the tx buffer, and nothing in the manual bounds a voucher by chain limits. 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs' concerns the honest operator's memory, not acceptance. 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8, unless ... an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)': here the referee model itself (Application) is what fails A5's converse, so it stays in scope. One reading puts it out of scope as 'what such an application gets, which is its outputs' if an application emitting a >55 KB voucher is deemed outside the interface; that needs a documented size bound, which does not exist.

2. Role: Application.executeOutput / LibBytes are part of 'cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 ... (input box, output validation)' = 'Referee model, as the deployed referee' (AUDIT.md). Section 3: 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.' It is not 'a defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond, or only crashes or stalls the model'.

3. High/Medium cases: none matches (not a verifier misbehaving only on unreachable states; not a divergence only at unreachable states; not a constant-factor R12 cost of an emulator operation). The per-byte copy alone could be argued as a constant-factor cost (~18x the calldata cost, High by analogy with 'multiply the worst-case cost ... by a constant factor'), but the listed constant-factor case is for operations listed in R12, which executeOutput is not.

4. Critical: it violates A5 at a reachable state: 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' The settled state commits to the voucher and a valid OutputValidityProof exists, but no transaction carrying it can be executed under the chain's per-transaction limits. Section 8 also lists as Critical 'An honest proof or transaction that cannot fit the chain's per-transaction limits, other than the delivery proof of an input that A3 requires the input record to refuse' - outputs have no such A3-like exemption. Section 1: 'accept an output that the settled state does not commit to' is the forward direction; this is the converse that A5 makes part of the obligation.

5. Low (alternative reading): if 'whenever its valid proof is presented' is read as conditional on the presentation fitting a transaction, the deployed referee accepts every presentable output and the defect is a missing documented output-size bound (manual/libcmt) plus a gas inefficiency, i.e. Low (or Medium as 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point' if the manual is read as promising that every voucher can be executed: 'Vouchers allow a Rolling Cartesi Machine to interact back with the blockchain ... grant a user the right to withdraw tokens'). Deciding facts: whether A5's converse covers presentability under per-transaction limits (section 8's Critical entry on transactions that cannot fit suggests it does), and whether the deployment documents a maximum output size.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (preferred: referee model violates A5's converse at a reachable state; section 8 'transaction that cannot fit the chain's per-transaction limits'). Alternative: Medium (manual/behavior contradiction) or Low (if presentability is outside A5).
candidates.threat_to_goal: Section 1 and A5 require that the referee accept every output the settled state commits to. Here a correctly designed application's committed voucher (e.g. a withdrawal right) can never be executed: the funds it authorizes stay locked. An input sender can provoke this for vouchers the application builds from input-controlled data. Note that the honest operator's claims are unaffected; the failure is purely in output acceptance.
candidates.evidence: Ran a forge test (scratch: GOALOUTPUT/gas/test/Gas.t.sol; foundry from bugs/harness/work/foundry/bin; no tracked file modified) that deploys the released Dave build's Application artifact (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/out/Application.sol/Application.json, via_ir+optimizer as Dave builds it) with a mock IOutputsMerkleRootValidator returning true, and calls executeOutput with Voucher(sink, 0, payload) outputs (payload mostly zero bytes, 1 nonzero byte per word), measuring the execution gas of the call: output 132 B -> 105,491; 1,156 B -> 406,106; 16,516 B -> 4,881,402; 45,188 B -> 13,371,647; 49,284 B -> 14,618,130; 53,380 B -> 15,873,103 (total with intrinsic 16,136,995); 57,476 B -> 17,137,103 (> 2^24); 65,668 B -> 19,495,411; 98,436 B -> 29,430,908; 131,204 B -> 39,561,177; 524,420 B -> 167,889,174; 2,097,092 B -> 814,895,078-828,598,323. Read libcmt v0.18.1-test1 src/rollup.c: emit_voucher/emit_delegate_call_voucher only fail when the encoding does not fit the tx buffer (2^21 bytes).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh runs a forge test (like Gas.t.sol) against the released Application artifact: build the largest voucher libcmt accepts (ABI encoding of length 2^21) or, for a smaller witness, a 64 KiB voucher, prove it with a mock validator (or a real outputs root of height 63), and assert that the total gas of executeOutput (execution + intrinsic, max(standard, EIP-7623 floor)) is <= 2^24 (EIP-7825 per-transaction cap) and the calldata <= the transaction size limit; exit 1 when it is not (today: 17.4 M at 57 KB, ~0.83 G at 2 MiB). The fixed behavior is either an execution path that fits every output the rollup interface allows, or a documented/enforced output-size bound in the manual and libcmt (emit refusing outputs whose execution would not fit), which the test would then check instead.

candidates.title: DaveConsensus never accepts outputs committed by a non-genesis template: isOutputsMerkleRootValid only knows roots of accepted epochs, while Application treats the template as the last finalized state
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 cartesi-rollups/contracts DaveConsensus (constructor, isOutputsMerkleRootValid) with cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application (_getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot fallback to TEMPLATE_HASH)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol: constructor (emits EpochSealed(0, ..., initialMachineStateHash, bytes32(0), ...) and records no outputs root), acceptStagedTournamentResult (the only writer of _outputsMerkleRoots), isOutputsMerkleRootValid; Application.sol _getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot (falls back to the template hash when the validator reports none).
candidates.description: A valid template may already commit to outputs (section 2: 'Its tx buffer holds the outputs Merkle root of every output that the application accepted before it, which at genesis is the root of the empty outputs tree'; A5: 'A valid template is such a state' from which an outputs root is defined). Until the first epoch is accepted, the template is the settled state - Application itself uses it as the last finalized machine state for withdrawals - but DaveConsensus.isOutputsMerkleRootValid returns false for the template's outputs root, because _outputsMerkleRoots is only written by acceptStagedTournamentResult and the constructor neither takes nor proves the template's root (a machine validity proof of the template would give it). Every valid proof of a template-committed output is refused during epoch 0 (the whole first tournament plus the staging period), and for ever if epoch 0 is never accepted: e.g. the guardian forecloses during epoch 0 (acceptStagedTournamentResult and stageTournamentResult are notForeclosed), or epoch 0 stalls. With foreclosure, withdrawals are then served from the template's accounts drive while the template's own outputs are never accepted.
candidates.trigger: Deployment of a Dave application from a template that commits to outputs (non-genesis template, e.g. a migrated application), then anyone presenting a template output's valid proof during epoch 0; the guardian (or an epoch-0 stall) makes the refusal permanent.
candidates.reachability: The template is a valid template by definition; no input is needed. The state is the deployment's initial settled state.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The permanent variant uses guardian foreclosure, whose role the threat model does not define; R1-A5-1 (foreclosure blocking acceptance of a finished tournament) was refuted, so that variant may be out of scope on the same reasoning. The delay variant needs no guardian. Not an application-design exclusion: the template is valid. If the deployment supports only genesis templates (empty outputs root), it is out of scope; the campaign's confirmed R2-DFOUTPUT-1 treats non-genesis templates as valid.
2. Role: DaveConsensus/Application are the referee model as deployed referee (AUDIT.md).

4. Critical reading: violates A5 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' at the initial settled state (the valid template), and permanently once epoch 0 cannot be accepted.

5. Low reading: if 'settled state' means only a state settled by a tournament, the template's outputs become acceptable once epoch 0 settles a state that commits to them (for a correctly designed application), and the defect is only a delay - Low. Deciding facts: whether the template counts as the settled state before epoch 0 (Application's own fallback says it does) and whether non-genesis templates are supported by Dave deployments.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low to Medium preferred (delay; permanent only with foreclosure or an epoch-0 stall); Critical under the reading that the template is the settled state and A5's converse applies to it.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Outputs that the initial settled state commits to are refused by the referee for the first epoch and possibly for ever, contrary to A5's converse; inconsistent with Application, which treats the same template as finalized.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: _outputsMerkleRoots is written only in acceptStagedTournamentResult; constructor emits outputs root bytes32(0) for epoch 0; Application._getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot falls back to TEMPLATE_HASH. No chain run.
candidates.test_idea: forge test on the released build: deploy DaveAppFactory/DaveConsensus with a template whose tx buffer holds a non-empty outputs root R0 (any valid template after one accepted output, e.g. the harness baremetal-template after one input), build an OutputValidityProof of output 0 against R0, and assert Application.validateOutput succeeds before epoch 0 is accepted (today it reverts InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot).

not_covered: No end-to-end chain run of stageTournamentResult/acceptStagedTournamentResult/executeOutput with a real machine validity proof and real outputs tree (gas measured with a mock validator only; the Application artifact is Dave's via_ir build, not necessarily the bytecode of the deployed ApplicationFactory).
Gas/size of stageTournamentResult and of executeOutput proofs themselves (3x59 and 63 siblings) were not measured; only the output-size dependence of executeOutput.
Dave Tournament internals that decide ROOT_WINNER and how finalState is authenticated were not re-read (taken from earlier rounds).
Orphaned inner tournaments calling provideMerkleRootOfInput with the next epoch's bounds after the root finished by timeout: only affects bonds, not outputs; not pursued.

Withdrawal path (proveAccountsDriveMerkleRoot/withdraw, accounts drive) and refund path (issueRefund, wasInputFinalized) were read for consistency with the last finalized state only; builders (RefundOutputBuilder, UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder) not read.
Delegate-call vouchers rewriting Application storage (_executed bitmap, validator, foreclosure flag): application-design choice, not pursued.
Sentry fast path (all sentries agree => no staging period) read only; no interplay with output acceptance found.

Recipe referee (prt.lua wait_for_outputs, game-output.lua) and vg.lua output acceptance: game-output.lua read and found consistent with Dave (fixed 63-sibling height, 32-byte target, per-epoch index set; single epoch so no cross-epoch duplicate); vg.lua not re-read.
PRT bridge/player encoding of MachineValidityProof/OutputValidityProof (prt-ethereum.lua, prt-bridge.lua) not read (support).
rollup-http-server and the rollup CLI output emission paths (output bytes hashed vs bytes declared in tohost) not re-read; libcmt emit/merkle read only for the size bound and pristine leaf (zero).
